# cato_allocated_ip (Resource)

Allocates an IP address from a Cato PoP location. Cato assigns the IP -- the configuration chooses the PoP location, description, and type; the resulting ip and display name ("Portland - 192.0.2.1") are computed and tenant-specific.

## Example Usage

```terraform
## Providers ###
provider "cato" {
  baseurl    = "https://api.catonetworks.com/api/v1/graphql2"
  token      = var.cato_token
  account_id = var.account_id
}

### Resource Usage ###

# Allocate an IP in a PoP location. Cato assigns the IP address --
# the configuration chooses the location, description, and type. The
# resulting ip and display name ("<pop> - <ip>") are computed.
resource "cato_allocated_ip" "portland" {
  pop_location_name = "Portland"
  description       = "AWS Bedrock Frontend"
}

# The description is the stable cross-tenant identity of an allocation
# (keep it unique per PoP location); policy rules reference the computed
# display name:
output "portland_allocation_name" {
  value = cato_allocated_ip.portland.name # e.g. "Portland - 199.27.34.88"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `pop_location_name` (String) Name of the Cato PoP location (city) to allocate the IP in, e.g. "Portland"

### Optional

- `description` (String) Description of the allocated IP (updatable in place). With pop_location_name, the cross-tenant identity of the allocation -- keep it unique per PoP location.
- `type` (String) Allocation type (SYSTEM is the only supported value today)

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Allocated IP identifier
- `ip` (String) The IP address Cato assigned to this allocation
- `name` (String) Display name of the allocation ("Portland - 192.0.2.1") as shown in entity lookups and referenced by policy rules

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import cato_allocated_ip.portland 199.27.34.88
```
